text:
maya: Heads-up: CVE-2026-0898 in libtls was flagged by the vuln scanner. Affects our inference runtime container. Patch landed upstream — we need a backport plan for Dedicated + Private where customers are on pinned images (VPC / on‑prem). Who can own the backport and packaging?

samir: I can take lead on the backport. Quick Q: does this require any RBAC or KMS schema changes? My read is it's a libs update but want confirmation.

olivia: quick triage: memory corruption during TLS handshake. No API change to our runtime. Upstream patch is just a dependency bump + recompile. We still need to rebuild, sign, and produce an onprem bundle with SBOM.

jordan: Note for Private on‑prem customers: their policies require signed artifacts and an offline bundle w/ manifest. That adds packaging + QA time. Also watch for audit log proof for KMS ops.

maya: Context: AcmeHealth is on a pinned branch with custom RBAC tweaks (they changed audit logging paths). They cannot accept a hosted rolling patch. We'll need a customer-specific backport to their pinned image. They also use an HSM with different key IDs — kms config can be brittle.

opsbot: deploy-bot: Canary pool for dedicated-us-west queued. Earliest deploy window: 2026-06-12 02:00 UTC.

samir: Plan: create branch hotfix/libtls-CVE-2026-0898 from the customer's pinned commit -> cherry-pick upstream patch -> rebuild -> sign -> produce onprem bundle + SBOM. Need registry mirror creds for Acme.

olivia: Build steps I'll follow (short):
```
git checkout -b hotfix/libtls-CVE-2026-0898 ACME/pinned-2026-05-14
git cherry-pick <upstream-commit>
make image
./scripts/sign-image.sh --key=acme-hsm-key
```
Also attach SBOM and upload artifact to secure S3.

jordan: KMS note: HSM signing can add latency and sometimes requires a key wrapper. Make sure sign script writes the KMS keyID into image labels: `com.redwood.kms.keyid=<id>` so Acme audit matches.

maya: Prioritization: AcmeHealth is HIPAA-regulated — mark P1 for their private deployment. For Dedicated customers mark P2 unless they escalate.

security-bot: vuln-tracker: CVE-2026-0898 created, severity: High, CVSS: 7.8. Affects runtime images <= v3.2.x. Suggested SLA: Dedicated: 72h; Private: 7d, but expedite for regulated customers.

samir: One blocker: Acme's RBAC disables hostPath mounts in their cluster. Our image build uses an ephemeral hostPath to stage certs. I'll rework the build to use tmpfs inside the container to avoid hostPath. That should not change runtime RBAC.

olivia: I'll open a PR against Acme's pinned branch with the patch and artifacts. PR checklist: SBOM, signed image digest, audit log proof, KMS keyID label, canary plan.

maya: I'll handle customer comms and draft the maintenance notice once PR is open.

jordan: After build/QA, ops will schedule the onprem maintenance window. For Dedicated we can do a rolling canary in us-west then global.

opsbot: deploy-bot: created ticket #OPS-4279 for AcmeHealth onprem rolling patch.

maya: Timeline ask: can we get Acme patched in 48h? Samir — is that doable?

samir: 48h is tight but possible if cherry-pick is clean and HSM signing goes smoothly. I'll begin now and post build link here.

olivia: I'll add audit capture to the build pipeline: run `auditd` inside the build job and upload logs to secure S3 with 1y retention per compliance.

maya: Thanks. Ping me when you need Acme registry creds or cross‑org approvals.

security-bot: incident-note: added to backport runbook: `verify signed image digest against customer KMS keyid` and `include audit log manifest` — automated checks added to CI.

samir: I'll post the hotfix branch + build artifact link when ready.

maya: Great — please @me once the PR is created.

(End)
